  PROBLEM: A reset 1 to 179 seconds in the future passes the `hours_left > 0` check but `:.1f` rounds it to `in 0.0h`, where "now" would be the right wording.
  WHY: The message shows a zero-hour countdown for a reset that has not happened yet; the effect is cosmetic and does not change gating, alerting or sending.
- scripts/claude_engine.py:836-839 | severity=nit | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `_window_summary` returns None early when utilization is missing, before it looks at the window's reset timestamp, while `window()` (lines 558-564) reads the two independently.
  WHY: A probe with a reset time but no utilization shows `5h ?` with no reset countdown, although the PR shows hours for every window with a known reset (the confidence=2 report came from anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, and the others gave 4).
- scripts/claude_engine.py:864-867 (pool_health docstring), changelog.d/8580-pool-reset-hours.md:10 | severity=nit | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The docstring and changelog describe `next_usable_in` as `in 0.8h` or empty, but `_format_reset_in` also returns `now` once the earliest reset has passed.
  WHY: The capacity-wait line in scripts/claude_pool_health_alert.sh can render `(now)`, a value the documented contract does not describe; nothing crashes.

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/claude_engine.py:814-821 | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A reset 1 to 179 seconds away rounds to `resets in 0.0h`, where "now" would be right.
  WHY: Cosmetic only; it does not change gating, alerting or sending.
- scripts/claude_engine.py:837-839 (and `window()` at line 558) | severity=nit | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: `_window_summary` returns before looking at `{name}_resets_at`, so a probe with a reset time but no utilization shows `5h ?` with no countdown.
  WHY: The reset time is not shown, but nothing in the diff shows such a probe occurring.
- scripts/claude_engine.py:864-866 (pool_health docstring), changelog.d/8580-pool-reset-hours.md (last line) | severity=nit | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `next_usable_in` is documented as `in 0.8h` or empty, but it can also hold `now`.
  WHY: Nothing crashes; a consumer parsing `in Xh` or empty would be surprised by `now`.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: The hourly alert "now lists every probed account, not only the gated ones", which changes the `CLAUDE_POOL_HEALTH` contract text.
  Expected change site: agents.md line 3953, the `CLAUDE_POOL_HEALTH` registry bullet in "Stable log prefixes (contractual)"; under §25 this is an in-place correction.
  Evidence of absence: agents.md:3953 still says `sent` means one Telegram WARNING named every account at or above `gate_utilization` and every rejected token; the PR has no agents.md edit and no `agents.d/` fragment.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- HARDENING: `_format_reset_in` line 821; set `shown = round(hours_left, 1)` and return `f"in {shown:.1f}h" if shown > 0 else "now"` (2 lines); HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/claude_engine.py:837-839 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `_window_summary` returns early when utilization is missing, without checking whether a reset timestamp exists.
  WHY: The reset countdown is not reported for that window even if the reset timestamp (e.g. five_hour_resets_at) is available.
- scripts/claude_engine.py:814-817 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The docstring documents reset countdowns as `in 0.8h` or empty, but omits the reachable `now` output.
  WHY: The documentation is inaccurate about the return contract of `_format_reset_in` once reset times have passed.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: The hourly alert now lists every probed account, not only the gated ones, so the agents.md contract text for the CLAUDE_POOL_HEALTH log prefix must be updated.
  Expected change site: agents.md, Stable log prefixes (contractual) section, CLAUDE_POOL_HEALTH registry entry.
  Evidence of absence: agents.md describes the entry as one that "named every account at or above gate_utilization and every rejected token", which is now incorrect, and no hunk in the PR touches agents.md.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- HARDENING: `_format_reset_in`; resets 1 to 179 seconds away format as `in 0.0h`. Fix: compute `shown = round(hours_left, 1)` and return `in {shown:.1f}h` if shown > 0 else `now` (2 lines); HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/claude_engine.py:837-839 (`window()` at 558-564, `parse_probe()` at 699-706) | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `_window_summary` returns immediately when utilization is missing, before checking the reset timestamp, while `parse_probe` stores the two independently.
  WHY: The report renders `5h ?` or `7d ?` and omits the reset countdown, despite the PR description requiring every window with a known reset to show one.
- scripts/claude_engine.py:820-821 | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A future reset less than about three minutes away is formatted as `in 0.0h`.
  WHY: The alert reports a nonzero wait as zero hours, although the code reserves `now` for passed reset times.
- changelog.d/8580-pool-reset-hours.md:10 (`scripts/claude_engine.py:820-821`, `scripts/claude_pool_health_alert.sh:84-88`) | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `next_usable_in` description lists `in 0.8h` or empty, but the implementation also returns `now`.
  WHY: The capacity-wait message can display `(now)`, which the documented output contract does not describe.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- scripts/claude_engine.py:814-822 | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A reset 1 to 179 seconds in the future passes the `hours_left > 0` check but formats to `in 0.0h`.
  WHY: The zero-hour countdown for a reset that has not happened contradicts the intent that "now" is reserved for passed resets; it is cosmetic only.
- scripts/claude_engine.py:836-839 (compare `window()` lines 558-564) | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When a probe carries a reset timestamp but no utilization for a window, `_window_summary` returns None and the countdown is omitted from both `pool_health` and `pool_usage_report` messages.
  WHY: An operator cannot see when the window resets; the line silently shows `5h ?` with no reset note.
- scripts/claude_engine.py:864-867 (pool_health docstring), changelog.d/8580-pool-reset-hours.md:10, versus `_format_reset_in` line 821 and `next_usable_in` at lines 906-908 | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The docstring and changelog document `next_usable_in` as `in 0.8h` or empty, but `_format_reset_in` also returns `now` and `next_usable_in` passes it through.
  WHY: scripts/claude_pool_health_alert.sh:85-88 can render `earliest reset 2026-11-01 01:00 UTC (now)`, a reachable value the documented contract does not describe; no crash.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: The PR changes the hourly near-cap alert from "names every account at or above `gate_utilization`" to "lists every probed account with both utilizations and the hours until each window resets", and the log-prefix registry in agents.md describes what a `sent` alert means.
  Expected change site: agents.md, "Stable log prefixes (contractual)", the `CLAUDE_POOL_HEALTH` registry bullet (agents.md:3953), via an in-place correction or an agents.d fragment.
  Evidence of absence: agents.md:3953 still reads "`sent` means one Telegram WARNING named every account at or above `gate_utilization` and every rejected token"; no PR hunk touches agents.md and no `agents.d/` fragment is in the changed-files list.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- HARDENING: `_format_reset_in` line 821; `shown = round(hours_left, 1)` then `return f"in {shown:.1f}h" if shown > 0 else "now"` (2 lines); HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
